messages.subject: mapmaker input of ril
parts:
Hello, 

I would like how to enter data into rqtl which was obtained by mapbuilding with onemap from a ril selfing population (F8). 

no matter what data type i enter in the rawfile, i get an error that it is an invalid cross type:

could you help me with that? 
Thank you, 
Michel

command used: 

test.qtl <- read.cross("mm", file = raw.file ,mapfile = "/home/moser/test")
Error in read.cross.mm(dir, file, mapfile, estimate.map) : 
  File indicates invalid cross type: bc.

messages.author: 65ee6740f5492ac2
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] mapmaker input of ril
parts:
Hi Karl, 

Thank you!

So in order to import a RIL population file in mm format (preliminary map built with onemap), could i import it as "backcross" and then change the cross description or is there no way to load such data in mm format? 
So i would have to load the raw data and transfer the marker order from the previous map manually with switch.order()? 

I am currently comparing ordering with different settings in rqtl and onemap. It looks like some of the maps actually get worse when increasing numbers of iterations and window-size.
Is it because it is stuck in an local optimum? 

Could you maybe give me some tips about optimising the orderMarkers() run? Or is it best to do this manually with some ripple() runs?

here some examples with my smallest linkage group:

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] mapmaker input of ril
parts: > So in order to import a RIL population file in mm format (preliminary map built with onemap), could i import it as "backcross" and then change the cross description or is there no way to load such data in mm format?

Either the file needs to be changed, or the code that produced it, or R/qtl.

I've changed R/qtl to handle such files (I think): https://github.com/kbroman/qtl/commit/d45c3866f
If you install the devtools package (and if you have the necessary tools, including a fortran compiler, for compiling source packages) you can install the revised version of R/qtl from GitHub:

install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("kbroman/qtl@devel")

> I am currently comparing ordering with different settings in rqtl and onemap. It looks like some of the maps actually get worse when increasing numbers of iterations and window-size.
> Is it because it is stuck in an local optimum?
>
> Could you maybe give me some tips about optimising the orderMarkers() run? Or is it best to do this manually with some ripple() runs?

I'd want to use a *much* larger value for window(), though it'd take a very long time with that density of markers.

The map construction tools in R/qtl are not very automated and not well suited for very large numbers of markers.

From the result that you're getting, it seems like the map needs to be folder over onto itself, at the center.

karl

messages.author: 65ee6740f5492ac2
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] mapmaker input of ril
parts:
Sorry, misunderstanding! The issue is not with the specification of the cross. One can easily change the naming of the data type from "backcross" to "bc" or whatever one prevers ...

I am worried about the underlying implications of stating a cross being backcrossed when it is actually a RIL (F7 selfed). 
It must have some effect on how the map building and rf calculation is done.

Restating the question: How do i read in data in mm-format of a RIL population into rQTL to get it treated correctly? 

Thank you, 
Michel

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] mapmaker input of ril
parts:
It shouldn't affect marker ordering, but only estimates of inter-marker distances.

When reading the data with read.cross, use the argument crosstype="riself".
Alternatively, after reading in the data, use convert2riself():

mycross <- convert2riself(mycross)

karl
